summary: Full backend + frontend testing of AI Administrative Verification (Verifikasi AI). Created /app/backend/tests/test_ai_verification.py with 6 pytest tests — all pass (19.7s). Coverage: (1) student RBAC returns 403 on GET list, POST generate, POST approve; (2) admin generate analyzes a complete controlled candidate → recommendation=recommended, document_count=10, approval_status=pending; (3) an incomplete controlled candidate → recommendation=review with populated issues list and registration status untouched (submitted); (4) approve selected updates only the chosen registration to lolos_administrasi, marks recommendation approved, creates selection_progress notification, and leaves other candidates untouched; (5) approve_all updates the remaining recommended pending candidate but leaves review-status candidates unchanged; (6) approve with empty payload returns 400; (7) super_admin can list. Direct-pymongo teardown removes all TEST_ai_verif users, profiles, documents, registrations, verification_recommendations, notifications, and the test campus — 50 seed students preserved (verified). Frontend: admin login → menu-verifikasi-ai renders ai-verification-manager; all required data-testids present (summary/total/recommended/review, filter-all/recommended/review, generate/approve-selected/approve-all, recommendation-*, approval-dialog, confirm-*); filter buttons switch views; approve-all correctly disabled when recommended count = 0; mobile 390px viewport has 0px horizontal overflow; student login does not render the verifikasi-ai menu.
critical_code_review_comments: verification_recommendations collection is upserted per user but never purged when a user/registration is deleted — over time stale 'review' rows accumulate and are displayed in the UI even for users that no longer exist (currently there are ~16 residual review rows from prior test iterations). Consider adding a cleanup step in the generate endpoint that deletes recommendations whose user_id is not present in the current registrations query, or a scheduled purge.

generate_verification_recommendations processes up to 5000 registrations but the AI call is issued in batches of 20 sequentially — for large cohorts this will time out under the current 60s default; consider asyncio.gather across batches with concurrency cap.

In ai_administration_recommendations the Gemini streaming call catches all exceptions and only logs a warning; if AI silently returns nothing, every candidate falls back to 'review' (correct fail-safe behaviour) but there is no visibility for admins that AI actually ran vs skipped. Consider surfacing 'ai_available: bool' in the generate response.
